4.note: These two phrases mean basically the same thing and emphasize that the people must obey everything that Yahweh has commanded them to do. You can translate this parallelism into one statement that conveys the requirement to keep all of Yahweh’s commands. Alternate translation: [You must obey all of my laws and commandments]

Obeying Yahweh’s commandments is spoken of as if they were a way or path that a person walks along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [so that you conduct your behavior according to them]

6.note: The phrase **to uncover nakedness** is a polite way of referring to sexual activity. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [to have sexual relations]

7.q: עֶרְוַ֥ת אָבִ֛י⁠ךָ וְ⁠עֶרְוַ֥ת אִמְּ⁠ךָ֖ לֹ֣א תְגַלֵּ֑ה
7.note: This is a polite way of referring to sexual activity. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [Do not have sexual relations with your father or your mother]
This is a polite way of referring to sexual activity. Alternate translation: [you must not have sexual relations with her]

8.note: Sometimes men had more than one wife. God did not allow a son to have sexual intercourse with any woman married to his father, even if she was not his mother.
Alternate translation: [You would dishonor your father]

9.q: עֶרְוַ֨ת אֲחֽוֹתְ⁠ךָ֤ בַת־אָבִ֨י⁠ךָ֙ א֣וֹ בַת־אִמֶּ֔⁠ךָ מוֹלֶ֣דֶת בַּ֔יִת א֖וֹ מוֹלֶ֣דֶת ח֑וּץ לֹ֥א תְגַלֶּ֖ה עֶרְוָתָֽ⁠ן
9.note: This is a polite way of referring to sexual activity. See how this is translated in Leviticus 18:7. Alternate translation: [Do not have sexual relations with your sister, the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother, born at home or born outside]
This means a man cannot have sexual intercourse with his sister even if she has a different mother or father.

10.note: Alternate translation: [for you will dishonor yourself as well as them]

11.note: This could mean: (1) “your half-sister” or (2) “your stepsister.” Here the man does not have the same father or mother as the woman. They became brother and sister when their parents married.

12.note: This is a polite way of referring to sexual activity. See how this is translated in Leviticus 18:7. Alternate translation: [Do not have sexual relations with your father’s sister]

14.note: You may have to make explicit the purpose of the approach. Alternate translation: [do not go to his wife in order to have sexual relations with her]

15.note: This is a polite way of referring to sexual activity. See how this is translated in Leviticus 18:7. Alternate translation: [Do not have sexual relations with your daughter-in-law]
This is a polite way of referring to sexual activity. Alternate translation: [You must not have sexual relations with her]

16.note: Alternate translation: [If you do that, you will dishonor your brother]

17.note: This is a polite way of referring to sexual activity. See how this is translated in Leviticus 18:7. Alternate translation: [Do not have sexual relations with a woman and her daughter]
Alternate translation: [to have sexual relations with her]

19.note: This refers to the time every month when a woman bleeds from her womb.
Alternate translation: [to have sexual relations with her]

21.note: The phrase **to pass over to Molech** refers to burning a child in the fire as a sacrifice to the idol Molech. Alternate translation: [You must not burn your children alive for Molech]
Here the word **name** represents God himself, and the word **profane** means “to dishonor.” Alternate translation: [And you must not dishonor your God]

22.note: This is a polite way of speaking of sexual relations. Use a polite way of referring to this in your language or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Do not have sexual relations with]
Here, **an abomination** refers to a violation of the natural order of things as Yahweh intended them to be.

23.note: This is a polite way of referring to sexual activity. Alternate translation: [to have sexual relations with it]

24.note: Here, **the nations** refers to the people groups already living in Canaan. Translate this so the term **nations** is clarified as people. Alternate translation: [the people of the nations … have defiled themselves]

25.note: Alternate translation: [And the people defiled the land]
Yahweh forcibly removing the people from the land is spoken of as if **the land vomited out the ones dwelling in it**. Alternate translation: [I forcibly removed the people from the land]
The **land** is spoken of as if it were a living thing that could vomit.

26.note: Alternate translation: [any of these disgusting things]

28.note: Yahweh forcibly removing the people from the land is spoken of as if the land **vomited** the people out. See how you translated this metaphor in Leviticus 18:25.
The land is spoken of as if it were a living thing that could **vomit**. See how you translated these phrases in Leviticus 18:25.

29.note: People who are excluded from the community are spoken of as if they had been **cut off** from their people, as one would cut a branch from a tree. Alternate translation: [the people who do these things must be separated from their people as a branch is cut from a tree]

If your language does not use the passive form, you could express this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you must separate those who do such things from their people]

30.note: If your language does not use the passive form, you could express this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [which the people did here before you came]
Here, **them** refers to the abominations and detestable customs.
